en.title: Lanterns' 'Lights Out' Delivers Heartbreak and Brutality Ahead of Netflix Debut
en.summary: A brutal showdown in 2007 sets the stage for future betrayals, while a devastating injury in 2016 reveals the fractured bonds within the Lantern Corps. This dark romance adaptation is shaping up to be a complex exploration of loyalty and sacrifice.
en.body:
Some breakups are tougher than others, and the latest installment of the Lanterns saga, "Lights Out," certainly proves that with a gut-wrenching look at fractured loyalties and brutal choices. The episode flashes back to 2007, introducing us to Kerry Kane arriving in Rushville, a marked woman pursued by Gotham enforcers. Her father’s alleged snitching has made her a target by association. Enter Zoe Macon, who intervenes with deadly force, demonstrating a ruthless pragmatism that shocks and impresses. To spare Kerry further harm, Zoe demands a gruesome sacrifice: her own pinky finger. This act of extreme self-mutilation, presented as a grim pact for future protection, immediately establishes the dark, morally ambiguous tone of the narrative. Zoe’s chilling assurance that fingers can regrow only adds to the unsettling nature of this nascent partnership.

The timeline then jumps to 2016, where the consequences of such alliances are starkly revealed. John Stewart finds himself critically injured, pinned by his leg after a car wreck. Hal Jordan arrives not with aid, but with an ultimatum. He declares his intention to usurp John’s position and bring in the Manhunter himself, now that John is incapacitated. Hal’s cold calculation extends to abandoning John and taking Zoe to Oa, effectively ending their partnership and training. John’s fury is palpable, but his severe injuries render him helpless. Sheriff Kane attempts to warn Hal about the futility of his plan, hinting at the deep-seated issues within Rushville that Hal seems dangerously unaware of.

## A Grim Pact Forged in Blood

This mid-season escalation in "Lights Out" serves as a crucial turning point, not just for the characters but for the overarching narrative of the **Lanterns** series. The stark contrast between the desperate, almost primal survival pact made in 2007 and the calculated betrayal witnessed in 2016 highlights the series' commitment to exploring the darker corners of its universe. The adaptation, based on Navessa Allen's bestselling dark romance novel from the **Into Darkness** series, is clearly leaning into the source material's intensity. Hannah Schneider, who penned the adaptation for Netflix, seems poised to deliver a story where personal connections are as dangerous as any external threat.

## The Fallout for Fans

For fans of Navessa Allen's work and newcomers alike, "Lights Out" promises a deep dive into complex character dynamics. The brutal efficiency with which Zoe Macon operates and the cold ambition displayed by Hal Jordan suggest a narrative that doesn't shy away from morally gray areas. The implications of John Stewart's injury and Hal's power grab are immense, potentially reshaping the entire Lantern Corps dynamic. This episode underscores the high stakes involved, making the wait for subsequent episodes all the more agonizing as viewers anticipate how these betrayals will unfold and how Kerry and John will navigate the treacherous paths laid before them.

## What's Next

The **Lanterns** series, adapted from Navessa Allen's **Lights Out**, continues its run on Netflix. Future episodes are expected to further explore the ramifications of the events in "Lights Out," delving deeper into the intertwined fates of Kerry Kane, Zoe Macon, John Stewart, and Hal Jordan.

Recap Image: John Johnson/HBO Max It’s 2007 and Kerry Kane has just arrived at the cafe on the outskirts of Rushville. She’s being followed by two henchmen from Gotham who are there to kill her because Kerry’s father was a snitch (likely against the mob), making her one by association. Zoe Macon appears and kills one of the men, then asks the other what needs to be done in order to leave Kerry alone. He tells her he’s supposed to go back to his boss with her finger to prove they killed her, so Zoe gives Kerry a knife and she cuts off her own pinky. After sending the man away with ample threats if he fails, Zoe explains that she did this for Kerry because she’s been in a similar position, and also because she expects the same defense in return when anyone comes after her in the future. Once Kerry agrees, Zoe says they can regrow her finger. It’s 2016 and John Stewart has been in a car wreck and is pinned to the dash by his leg. Hal Jordan approaches to let John know that he’s not about to let the man take his job, and that he’s going to be bringing in the Manhunter himself, now that John is suitably out of the picture; he’ll get Antaan and his men to fight off Macon’s militia while he takes Zoe to Oa—their partnership and training is ended. John is understandably furious, but he’s too injured to be able to do anything about it. Hal leaves him there and goes to find Sheriff Kane, who tries to explain that this isn’t going to work out for Hal: everyone in Rushville is required to defend Zoe and will, meaning that he’s likely to die and wreck carnage on the entire town in the process. She fires on Hal repeatedly while he shields himself with the ring, noting that Zoe knows what everyone is doing, and a hit is bound to be put out on Hall shortly. Zoe finds John in the car but neglects to save him before it explodes. She has him brought to the hospital, where it’s revealed that he has burns all over his body. Zoe makes John a deal: She’ll repair his injuries if he agrees to fight for her. Once she kills Hal, he will become the Green Lantern and tell the Guardians that she’s dead. She knows he doesn’t trust the Guardians any more than she does. John has figured out that the Guardians made the Manhunters, and hasn’t truly been on board since learning that they expected him to take the ring off of Hal… but he also knows that Zoe killed Abin Sur, the previous Green Lantern, despite the fact that he brought her to Earth to save her life. Image: John Johnson/HBO Max John agrees to Zoe’s terms, letting her know that if her regeneration machine makes him white, the deal is off.
